summary: Frontend-only verification of the new 'Clear Code' button (data-testid='clear-code-btn') across all 5 editor pages. Tested behavior end-to-end on AssignmentPage, LessonPageTemplate (existing Reset button), and TeacherPractice using admin credentials — all 3 pages show the confirm dialog with the correct message, dismissing keeps the user's edits, accepting resets to the problem's starter_code (or the fallback '# Write your code here\n' if none). StudentSandbox and CodingTestTaking were verified via code inspection only (see notes) because they require a student session; both are correctly wired to window.confirm + setCode and CodingTestTaking's Clear does NOT touch the submission counter. Run Code button is still present alongside Clear on every page.

The student-side editor (run-code-btn, line ~1588) still has no Clear button. critical_code_review_comments: resetCode.js helper is clean, single-purpose, ~30 lines — good.
No hardcoded URLs, uses window.confirm which is standard cross-browser.
The helper returns false when currentCode already equals target — nice UX (silent no-op).
All 4 injected buttons use consistent styling (Trash2 icon + 'Clear' label + variant='outline' + size='sm') and correctly disable while running/submitting/finalized. Good consistency.
AssignmentPage.jsx is 2335 lines — flagged in prior iterations, still not split. Not blocking for this feature.

In StudentSandbox.jsx line 77 the confirm() is inlined instead of using the shared resetCodeWithConfirm helper. Slight DRY violation — the sandbox also resets output+testInput and shows a toast, which is why it wasn't refactored. Acceptable, but consider extending the helper with an optional afterReset callback for future consistency.
